content.question:
Imagine a page contains:

- a page heading
- a search area
- a list of products
- one repeated product row

Which piece is the strongest candidate for a reusable component?

feedback.correct: Repeated or meaningful UI pieces are good component boundaries because a named component can describe that piece once and reuse it.
feedback.incorrect: Repeated or meaningful UI pieces are good component boundaries because a named component can describe that piece once and reuse it.

content.title: What should become a component?
content.text:
A common beginner trap is splitting everything into tiny components just because it is possible.

A better question is:

**Does this piece have a meaningful responsibility, reuse, or boundary?**

You do not need a component for every `<span>`.

content.question: Which design is easier to change later?

options.text: One giant component containing every product row separately.
A page component that composes a reusable product component.

feedback.correct: A meaningful component boundary lets one change update all uses of that piece.
feedback.incorrect: A meaningful component boundary lets one change update all uses of that piece.
